label: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
definition: A theorem in calculus with two parts connecting differentiation and integration: Part 1 establishes that a definite integral function is an antiderivative; Part 2 (the evaluation theorem) evaluates a definite integral using any antiderivative.

scope.text: Calculus; real-valued functions continuous on a closed interval [a,b]
scope.basis: as-stated for continuity conditions; broader calculus scope inferred

notes: Named theorem as a Concept anchor. The two parts are distinct theorem Statements. Proofs are recorded as reusable Procedures plus specific Study derivations.
